question:
A particle moves along a straight line such that its displacement after $t$ seconds is $s(t)=t^4-4t^3+4t^2$ metres, where $t\geq 0$.

(a) Obtain expressions for its instantaneous velocity and acceleration.

(b) Determine the positive instants at which the particle is at rest.

(c) Find the acceleration at each of these instants.

(d) Examine the direction of motion in the intervals determined by these instants.
explanation:
(a)
The instantaneous velocity is the rate of change of displacement with respect to time.
$$v(t)=\frac{ds}{dt}=4t^3-12t^2+8t$$
$$v(t)=4t(t-1)(t-2)$$
The acceleration is the rate of change of velocity.
$$a(t)=\frac{dv}{dt}=12t^2-24t+8$$

(b)
The particle is at rest when $v(t)=0$. Therefore,
$$4t(t-1)(t-2)=0$$
Thus, $t=0$, $t=1$ or $t=2$. The required positive instants are
$$t=1\ \text{second}\quad\text{and}\quad t=2\ \text{seconds}$$

(c)
At $t=1$,
$$a(1)=12(1)^2-24(1)+8=-4\ \text{m/s}^2$$
At $t=2$,
$$a(2)=12(2)^2-24(2)+8=8\ \text{m/s}^2$$

(d)
For $00$.
For $1For $t>2$, all three factors are positive. Hence, $v(t)>0$.
Therefore, the particle moves in the positive direction for $02$.
